business_scope.primary_industry_name: Retailing of Smart IoT Devices and Home Automation

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Colombia (single national unitary jurisdiction; no sub-state tax autonomy)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Romano-Germanic tradition; unitary code-based system under the Colombian Civil Code of 1887 and the Código de Comercio of 1971)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Colombia-United States Trade Promotion Agreement (in force 2012)
Colombia-European Union Multi-Party Trade Agreement (provisionally applied since 2013; ratified by Colombia)
Colombia-United Kingdom Continuity Trade Agreement (in force 2021)
Colombia-Spain Reciprocal Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (in force)
Colombia-Netherlands Agreement on Encouragement and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (in force)
Colombia-South Korea Free Trade Agreement (in force 2016)
Pacific Alliance Framework Agreement (Colombia, Chile, Mexico, Peru; in force)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: AML/CFT and UBO regime: Ley 526 de 1999 (creates the Financial Information and Analysis Unit UIAF); Ley 1121 de 2006 (counter-terrorist financing); Ley 1762 de 2015 (AML reform laundering and self-laundering); Ley 2277 de 2022, Article 16 (creates the Registro Unico de Beneficiarios Finales RUB administered by DIAN with implementing conditions in DIAN Resolucion 000164 de 2023; tax-oriented UBO identification threshold is 5% of capital, profit rights or control); Decreto 1674 de 2016 and Decreto Unico 1068 de 2015, Part 2.1.4 (beneficial-owner definition and non-financial-sector AML obligations; FATF-aligned 25% threshold for obliged-entity customer due diligence institutions); Circular Unica de la Superintendencia Financiera (Circular Basica Juridica), Parte II, Titulo IV - SARLAFT as updated by Circular 029 de 2018 and Circular 037 de 2021; Superintendencia de Sociedades Circular 004 de 2022 (SAGRILAFT for supervised non-financial entities once asset or income thresholds are exceeded). For the proposed S.A.S. engaged in low-risk online IoT retail and holding no statutory license, the directly mandatory layer at pre-incorporation consists of the DIAN RUB filing linked to the future NIT, the standard banking and PSP AML/CFT due-diligence package required at account opening and Stripe/Shopify Payments onboarding, and preparation for SARLAFT/SAGRILAFT once the company crosses the applicable compliance thresholds.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or certificate of existence of the foreign parent/shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry in the country of origin (e.g., Companies House, Secretary of State, local Chamber of Commerce of the parent jurisdiction)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Colombia is a party to the Hague Apostille Convention of 5 October 1961, ratified by Ley 455 de 1998, in force since 30 January 2001); if the origin jurisdiction is not a Hague member, Colombian Consular Legalization is required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board resolution of the foreign parent authorizing the incorporation of the Colombian S.A.S. and the appointment of its legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary or notary of the foreign parent jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or, in non-Hague jurisdictions, Colombian Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney (poder) granted by the foreign parent to the local incorporation agent or designated representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or, in non-Hague jurisdictions, Colombian Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO declaration and certified identification documents (passport copies) of each final beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or competent certification authority in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or, in non-Hague jurisdictions, Colombian Consular Legalization

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law 1258 of 2008 (Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada), Art. 5 and 17; Colombian Commercial Code, Art. 110 et seq.; Law 1429 of 2010 (formalization incentives)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio of the company's registered jurisdiction, under the supervision of the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución (private incorporation document) filed for mercantile registration, or public deed if real property is contributed
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital; capital is freely set in the bylaws. At least 20% of the subscribed value of each share must be paid at incorporation; the balance must be paid within one year. Payment may be evidenced by a deposit in an escrow or ordinary bank account opened in the company's name.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF THE SOLE SHAREHOLDER — By unanimous written consent, it is resolved: (1) The share subscription offers set forth in the bylaws are accepted in full, and the minimum 20% paid-in capital is satisfied through the escrow bank deposit reference annexed; (2) The registered office is adopted at Calle 10 # 3-15, Bogotá D.C., Colombia, within the registry jurisdiction; (3) The shareholders appoint [Name] as Legal Representative and [Name] as Alternate Legal Representative, conferring broad powers to negotiate, sign contracts, open bank accounts, obtain permits, and represent the company before authorities; (4) The representatives are authorized to execute all filings necessary for mercantile registration, tax registration, and municipal licenses.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certificate of Name Availability and Homonym Check
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio – Online Homonym Registry (Registro Único Empresarial)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit three proposed corporate names to the Chamber of Commerce's online name-search system. The system verifies that the requested name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered company. The applicant receives an unofficial certificate of homonymy valid for 30 calendar days.
required_dossiers: Valid identification document of the shareholder or its legal representative
Completed homonym y search application form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, the applicant may resubmit a new name or appeal the rejection to the Chamber of Commerce's legal office within 5 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of the Incorporation Document
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría (Notary Public) if public deed is required; otherwise authorized signatory before the Chamber of Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the private incorporation document containing the bylaws, share subscription list, registered office address, and officers. If the company contributes real property or the subscribed capital exceeds the statutory threshold, the document must be executed as a public deed before a notary. Otherwise the private document is signed by the shareholder and the legal representative, with legalization of signatures before the Chamber of Commerce.
required_dossiers: Name availability certificate
Draft bylaws and incorporation document
Identification documents and taxpayer stamp (RUT) of signing parties
Proof of initial capital payment or bank deposit certificate, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses authentication, correct the identified defects and re-submit; if the private document is defective, the parties may execute a corrective amendment (aclaración) before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Mercantile Registration with the Chamber of Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio – Mercantile Registration Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the signed incorporation document, by-laws, and the completed registration form (Pre-RUT). Pay the registration fee, which is determined by the subscribed capital and the number of associates. Upon successful scrutiny, the Chamber issues the Business Existence Certificate (Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal).
required_dossiers: Signed incorporation document or notarial deed
Name availability certificate
Pre-RUT registration form
List of shareholders and officers with identification
Bank proof of initial paid-up capital, if required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry rejects or suspends the filing, the petitioner must correct the observations and resubmit within 10 business days; judicial recourse may be filed with the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio against improper rejection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Identification and Registration with DIAN
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales) – Online RUT portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the Business Existence Certificate, request the NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria) and the RUT (Registro Único Tributario) through the DIAN web portal. The legal representative must authenticate with their digital certificate or by personal appearance. Update the RUT with the ISIC 4791 economic activity, registered office, and responsible VAT status.
required_dossiers: Business Existence Certificate
Identification and RUT of the legal representative
Power of attorney, if filing through an agent
Email and mobile contact for electronic notification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RUT is rejected due to inconsistencies in the address or economic classification, the representative must correct the data online or in person at DIAN and re-apply immediately; an administrative appeal is available within 5 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Opening Permit and Bank Account Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alcaldía (Municipal Mayor's Office) / Cámara de Comercio / financial entity
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the commercial establishment (matrícula mercantil del establecimiento) once the company's main registered office is physically established. Request the municipal zoning certificate (uso de suelo compatible) and pay the industry and commerce tax (ICA) registration. Open the corporate bank account in the company's name and deposit any remaining subscribed capital. The business may begin operations upon obtaining the commercial opening permit.
required_dossiers: Business Existence Certificate and RUT
Lease agreement or ownership title of the office/retail premises
Zoning certificate or certificate of compatible land use
Fire inspection certificate, if applicable
ICA registration form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipal authority denies the opening permit due to zoning, apply for a land-use variance or choose a conforming location; if the fire inspection fails, remedy the cited deficiencies and resubmit within 10 business days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio (consumer protection and retail compliance); municipal Mayor's Office for commercial opening permits
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Matrícula Mercantil del Establecimiento (Commercial Opening and Establishment Registration)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente y Desarrollo Sostenible / Corporación Autónoma Regional (CAR)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from full EIA; registration as an electronic waste generator (Law 1672 of 2013 and Decree 284 of 2018) is required for retail of IoT hardware
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater or stack emissions from retail storage; any incidental electronic waste must be transferred to authorized WEEE recyclers. If future product testing occurs, compliance with Resolution 0631 of 2015 effluent thresholds and national air emission standards applies.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the delegated municipal fire department (Cuerpo de Bomberos) under Law 1575 of 2012; structural load inspection for the commercial retail premises; workplace safety clearance (SGSST) under Resolution 0312 of 2019.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: DIAN – Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (National Directorate of Taxes and Customs), portal: www.dian.gov.co; digital services via the Muisca and the VUCE (Foreign Trade Single Window).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity establishing a Colombian S.A.S. must (1) incorporate before a notary and the Chamber of Commerce to obtain the Certificado de Cámara de Comercio; (2) apply for the NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria) through the RUT (Registro Único Tributario) online at DIAN's Muisca portal, presenting the certificate of existence, foreign tax identification proof, and a local authorized representative's identification; (3) obtain digital signature certificate for e-invoicing and regulatory filings; (4) register as VAT responsible person (Régimen Común/Responsable de IVA), as importer/exporter (Usuario Aduanero) if conducting direct foreign trade, and as employer if hiring local staff.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid mismatch elections exist under Colombian tax law; corporate income tax (CIT) is assessed at the entity level on worldwide income for resident S.A.S. entities. Optional regimes include: (a) Régimen Simple de Tributación (SIMPLE) – a presumptive/aggregate tax election for qualifying small taxpayers under 100,000 UVT of gross revenue, integrating income tax, VAT, and municipal tax (ICA) burdens; (b) Grandfathering for newly incorporated entities is limited to a single reduced CIT rate on initial-year small profits for certain start-up entities (Ley 2010/2019, Art. 240-1), subject to strict thresholds and activity restrictions; (c) entities achieving export income may file for VAT refunds using the 'Exportador' certification procedure rather than an elective classification election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA (Value Added Tax / VAT) under Estatuto Tributario (Tax Code), Titles IV and V; complementary consumption taxes (Impuesto al Consumo) for specific goods/services
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No monetary threshold for VAT registration by importers, exporters, or persons engaged in the supply of taxable services/goods in commercial premises. Registrants under the ordinary 'Responsable de IVA' regime must register regardless of turnover. Simplified sales-regime status (Régimen Simplificado) is available only to natural persons (not to the S.A.S. corporate entity) if prior-year gross income < 3,500 UVT (approx. COP 152,000,000 for FY2025) and other asset/contract conditions are met; a registered S.A.S. always files as a 'Gran Contribuyente' or ordinary responsible taxpayer. Foreign digital service providers without a Colombian fixed place of business must register for IVA through the simplified non-resident regime once they have any Colombian customer (no de-minimis threshold).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time electronic invoicing (Facturación Electrónica) for all VAT responsible taxpayers with DIAN's Muisca web services, requiring: (1) XML invoice generation and immediate transmission/validation in DIAN's fiscal cloud before the sale is legally consummated; (2) 'CUFE' (Código Único de Facturación Electrónica) for standard invoices or 'CUDE' for equivalent documents, embedded with a digital stamp/QR code; (3) mandatory use of an approved software provider (Proveedor Tecnológico) or DIAN's free tool; (4) tax authority pre-validation of invoice request numbers; (5) electronic dispatch and receiving of invoices through DIAN's platform; (6) for e-commerce, integration with Shopify/Stripe payment gateways to issue automated e-invoices through certified APIs; failure to transmit or validate invoices triggers non-deductibility of expenses, penalties under Art. 652 E.T., and possible closure of establishment.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of tangible goods (including IoT hardware) are treated as zero-rated ('excluidas' with entitlement to input VAT credit/refund) under Art. 481 E.T., provided the goods physically leave Colombia and are sold to a foreign recipient. Eligible service exports, including digital support, software design, and cloud/after-sales services that are part of the smart-home IoT business, are zero-rated if they meet the 'servicios de exportación' criteria of Art. 481(b) E.T.: the service is rendered to a foreign entity, is utilized exclusively abroad, and the benefit/risk is transferred abroad; for marketing or digital services, the recipient must be a foreign non-resident and the service must generate export income. The zero-rating is not automatic; the taxpayer must prove actual foreign currency collection and the economic reality of the export through documentary evidence.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Forma Única de Exportación / Declaración Electrónica de Exportación (DEX)
Bill of Lading (for maritime) or Air Waybill (for air) evidencing physical dispatch from Colombian customs
Commercial invoice matching goods description, HS codes, and values
Packing list and certificate of origin (if applicable)
Certificado de Exportación (issued by customs broker/presented with DIAN VAT refund application)
Bank proof of foreign currency repatriation (Formas 1, 2, or 3 or intermediary bank statements showing FX settlement)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DIAN rigorously audits export VAT refunds; false or unsupported zero-rating claims trigger: (a) immediate reversal of the refund plus default interest (intereses moratorios) from the refund payment date; (b) penalty of 100% of the tax improperly refunded (Art. 648 E.T.); (c) additional penalty of 10% of the claimed value for inaccurate documentation; (d) criminal prosecution for tax fraud (Art. 434A E.T. – Defraudación Fiscal) and for false export claims under the Customs Regime Law 1762/2015, with imprisonment up to 9 years and fines; (e) registration on the DIAN enforcement blacklist and cancellation of the exporter authorization.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República de Colombia (Banrep) acting through the Oficina de Cambios under Law 9 of 1991, Decree 1068 of 2015 (Compilation of Foreign Exchange Regulations), and Circular Regulatory (DR) 21 of 2020.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Colombian peso (COP) is fully convertible for current-account trade in goods and services. Capital-account inflows and outflows require registration with Banco de la República and must be channelled through the Mercado Cambiario Institucional (MCI) via authorised intermediaries. Profit remittance is permitted for registered foreign investment after submitting the annual declaration of foreign investment (Declaración de Cambio) and satisfying tax clearance (e.g., DIAN certificate), subject to a withholding tax of 7.5% on dividends unless reduced by a tax treaty. Non-resident shareholders may hold 100% of SAS capital.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For exports of goods, proceeds must be collected within six months from the customs declaration date (unless an extension is granted) and 100% of the proceeds must be surrendered to the MCI, converting foreign currency into COP. The surrender must occur within five calendar days of collection. Exemptions apply for exports of certain services (e.g., software, call centres) where proceeds may be retained in foreign currency subject to registration. Late surrender attracts fines and sanctions under the foreign-exchange regime.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Local SEDPE (Sociedad Especializada en Depósitos y Pagos Electrónicos) licences permit account issuance and payment processing in COP; however, these entities cannot hold foreign currency or offer full cross-border deposit services. Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Wise, Airwallex, Revolut Business) are not authorised as credit institutions in Colombia and cannot replace a local treasury account. Feasibility for treasury holding: LOW. Use as an ancillary settlement rail only, not as the primary local treasury account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical appearance of directors is not mandatory if the SAS appoints a legal representative resident in Colombia with a valid cédula or resident visa. Most Tier-1 banks permit remote account opening with notarised and apostilled constitutional documents, a notarised power of attorney, and a senior compliance interview via videoconference. However, a biometric verification of the legal representative at a local notary or bank branch is commonly required. Non-resident directors can delegate authority and need not travel, but all corporate signature powers must be legally authenticated.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owner resident in a non-FATF jurisdiction with high terrorist-financing risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised and apostilled certificate of incorporation and bylaws; current certificate of representation issued by the Colombian Chamber of Commerce (Cámara de Comercio) within 30 days; valid passports and proof of residence of founders; CBG (Certificado de Beneficiario) listing all ≥10% owners; AML questionnaires and source-of-funds declaration; bank references from prior institutions; corroborating corporate bank statements for the first 3 months of operations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of digital payment platforms (Stripe, Shopify) generating cross-border funds without clear trade documentation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed e-commerce service agreements with payment processors, sample invoices and purchase orders, website domain registration with matching company details, annual projected transaction volumes, customs records (if applicable), and a signed sworn statement on the lawful origin of funds. Prohibited to accept third-party or cash deposits.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction for the counterparty supplier of IoT hardware (if source in certain Asia/MEA zones)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full KYC file of the supplier (business licence, passport of beneficial owner), commercial contract with terms, customs documentation (Bill of Lading, DIAN import declaration), and an independent open-source negative news review. The bank may require a written explanation of the import model and known supplier registration in the Single Registry of Importers.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound equity capital from non-resident shareholders must be routed as a SWIFT MT103 wire transfer to the local bank referencing the purpose code 324 ('Capital investment in local companies'). The bank must receive a notarised board resolution (acta) authorising capital increase, and the funds must be declared on the Formulario de Declaración de Cambio (Form For 3) and entered into the Registro de Inversiones Extranjeras within 6 months via the Oficina de Cambios. For the first injection, a notarised copy of the SAS's incorporation certificate and the shareholder's banking references are required. Funds must remain in the MCI and be converted to COP unless retained in foreign currency for operational needs (subject to limits).
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier payments for IoT hardware under retail import model are effected via SWIFT MT103 using purpose code 430 ('Imports of goods') and the corresponding DIAN customs declaration (Declaración de Importación) must be presented. For high-value transactions (>USD 10,000), a commercial letter of credit (L/C) may be required by the local bank. Operational disbursements for marketing or software subscriptions use purpose code 430 (services) with underlying contracts. All outbound foreign-currency payments must be settled through the MCI and reported in the Declaración de Cambio; the bank will verify the trade rationale and may request invoices, shipping documents, and the importer's registration.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward FX contracts (COP/USD) with local authorised banks for hedging purchase costs if the invoice currency is foreign
FX options (COP/USD) purchased from Tier-1 banks for critical trade flows
Cross-currency swaps (COP/USD) for investment capital conversion over multi-year operations

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) executed with offshore counterparties are not permitted for local accounts; local entities may only hedge through the MCI and with authorised intermediaries. If an NDF is essential, a formal request to Banco de la República (Oficina de Cambios) must be submitted with evidence of underlying exposure; approval is exceptional.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Renewal of Commercial Registry Registration (Renovación del Registro Mercantil)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local Chamber of Commerce (Cámara de Comercio) with jurisdiction over the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal after March 31 triggers a surcharge/fine calculated on the applicable renewal tariff; continued failure to renew exposes the company to administrative strike-off and loss of legal standing with the Chamber of Commerce.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements and Approving Shareholders' Meeting Minutes (Estados Financieros y Acta de Asamblea de Accionistas)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio with jurisdiction over the statutory situs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Financial statements for fiscal year ending December 31 must be approved by the shareholders by March 31; filing of approved statements with the Chamber must occur within one month after approval, generally by April 30.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file audited/approved financial statements by the applicable deadline may lead to fines by the Superintendencia de Sociedades, loss of the commercial registry validity, and evidentiary disadvantage in legal proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ordinary Shareholders' Meeting Minutes Record (Acta de Asamblea General Ordinaria)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate minute book (Libro de Actas) kept at the registered office; notarized copy filed when required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The ordinary meeting must be held at least once a year, normally during the first three months of the year; minutes must be recorded within 30 days after the meeting.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Absence of lawful minutes is a register irregularity that can trigger inspection, administrative penalties, or the appointment of a third-party auditor by the Superintendencia de Sociedades.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Income Tax Return (Declaración de Renta) and RUT Update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax and Customs Administration (DIAN — Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing window is based on the taxpayer's NIT check digit; in practice falling due between April and May of each fiscal year, as published in DIAN's annual calendar.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing produces statutory late-payment fines and default interest; persistent non-compliance may lead to tax seizure, administrative penalties, and criminal referral for tax evasion.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Owner (UBO) Confirmation and Update in the RUT
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN through the RUT (Registro Único Tributario); any changes also recorded in the Chamber of Commerce records where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: UBO data must be confirmed annually at the time of the RUT annual update, and updated within 15 days of any shareholding transfer or change in ultimate beneficial ownership.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Incomplete, inaccurate, or untimely UBO disclosure may result in fines imposed by DIAN, suspension of RUT status, and heightened AML-KYC scrutiny of the company's bank and payment providers.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A S.A.S. must appoint a statutory auditor (Revisor Fiscal) where its gross assets or gross revenues exceed the legal thresholds set by Colombian regulations (currently 3,000 times the monthly minimum legal wage, SMMLV, as annually indexed), or when such audit is expressly required by the bylaws; otherwise the audit is optional for smaller S.A.S. entities.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted in Colombia (NIIF); entities meeting Group 1 criteria apply full NIIF, while lower-tier S.A.S. entities apply NIIF para Pymes (IFRS for SMEs) under Decree 2420 of 2015.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Colombian law requires S.A.S. companies to identify and disclose their ultimate beneficial owners to DIAN through the RUT. This information must be confirmed on an annual basis and updated immediately upon any shareholding transfer or ownership change that alters beneficial control; the annual confirmation is typically embedded in the mandatory RUT update cycle.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$2,000–7,000 per certified annual audit (when compulsory or electively adopted)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 35% flat corporate income tax (Art. 240 ET) for FY 2023 and subsequent years; the rate was 30% in 2020, 31% in 2021 and 35% from 2022 onward.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays or preferential sectoral rate for retail trade. Effective reliefs: (i) deduction of ordinary and necessary expenses (COGS for IoT inventory, warehouse rent, salaries, cloud/SaaS subscriptions, merchant fees charged by Stripe/Shopify, logistics); (ii) tax depreciation on IT equipment and fixtures; (iii) the 3% advance income tax withholding on e-commerce retail sales (Art. 365-1 ET) is creditable against the annual CIT; (iv) municipal ICA paid is deductible. Tax losses do not expire (indefinite carryforward) but the annual offset is capped at 5% of the taxable income of each recovery year (Art. 147 ET); the schema numeric field of 5 denotes that annual cap, not a 5-year expiry.
